name: Anguilla Residence by Investment (Anguilla Economic Residence Act 2019)
notes: Permanent residence through approved real estate (US$750,000 for a family of four, 5-year hold) or a contribution to the Capital Development Fund (US$150,000 single applicant; not usable until the fund was set up, after December 2022). Run by the Select Anguilla Agency through authorised agents. A retroactive route covered owners of property bought before 31 May 2019 (US$500,000-750,000 depending on purchase date). The same Act offers tax residence (US$75,000 a year). An amending Act and Regulations were passed in 2024 (not retrieved). Permanent residence does not give Belonger status; naturalisation needs years of residence. No counts found.

name: UAE citizenship by nomination for investors and talents (amended Executive Regulation of Federal Law No. 17 of 1972 on Nationality and Passports)
notes: Not a citizenship-by-investment programme with a price: candidates (investors who own UAE property, doctors, scientists, inventors, artists, and their families) cannot apply; they are nominated by Rulers' and Crown Princes' courts, executive councils or the Cabinet. Dual nationality allowed; citizenship can be withdrawn if conditions are breached. No numbers of grants have been published. Announced by WAM on 30 Jan 2021; the amended regulation itself was not found.

name: UAE Golden Visa (الإقامة الذهبية - golden residence; long-term residence for investors, entrepreneurs and talents)
notes: Long-term residence without a sponsor. Created by Cabinet Resolution 56/2018 (in force 3 Feb 2019; permits issued from 21 May 2019): investors AED 10 million (10 years) or AED 5 million in property (5 years). Replaced by Cabinet Resolution 8/2021 (text not found), then by the annex to Cabinet Resolution 65/2022 (in force 3 Oct 2022): 10-year permits, AED 2 million in property, bank deposit or company share, or AED 250,000 a year in taxes. Issued by ICP federally and by GDRFA in Dubai. Gives no path to citizenship: there is no residence period that leads to naturalisation; citizenship is only by nomination (see are-citizenship-nomination). Official counts are press figures covering all golden-visa categories, mostly Dubai only; no investor-only series is published.

name: Argentina citizenship by investment (Ley de Ciudadanía 346, art. 2 inc. 2, as amended by Decreto 366/2025)
notes: Legal basis exists but no operating programme was found. Decree of necessity and urgency 366/2025 (28 May 2025) lets foreigners who make a "relevant investment" naturalise regardless of residence and creates the Agencia de Programas de Ciudadanía por Inversión under the Ministry of Economy; Decreto 524/2025 sets the procedure; Ley 27802 (2026) settles tax residence of such citizens; the Agency got an executive director from 22 Apr 2026. The Ministry of Economy has to define what counts as a relevant investment: no such resolution was found in the Boletín Oficial up to 1 Oct 2026, so there are no published amounts. Whether Congress has reviewed or rejected the DNU was not checked.

name: Argentina temporary residence as investor (residencia temporaria, subcategoría inversionista: Ley de Migraciones 25.871 art. 23; Decreto 616/2010, Anexo art. 23 d)
notes: Temporary residence for a foreigner making a productive, commercial or service investment of interest to the country of at least ARS 1,500,000 (fixed in pesos in the 2010 decree), with proof of the lawful origin of the funds and their entry through banks authorised by the central bank, and a non-binding opinion of the industry ministry on the project. Distinct from the 2025 citizenship-by-investment route (arg-cbi). Launch shown as the date of the regulatory decree; the subcategory exists in the 2004 law. No official counts found; later changes to the amount not found in this pass.

name: Antigua and Barbuda Citizenship by Investment Programme (CIP)
notes: Set up by the Citizenship by Investment Act 2013 (gazetted 11 Apr 2013); run by the Citizenship by Investment Unit (CIU). Routes: National Development Fund donation, real estate, business investment, and (from 2018) University of the West Indies Fund. 5,203 applications from inception to 30 Jun 2024.

name: Business Innovation and Investment Program (BIIP): Business Innovation and Investment (Provisional) visa subclass 188, (Permanent) subclass 888, Business Talent subclass 132
notes: Umbrella programme for business and investor migrants under the Migration Regulations 1994. Provisional (subclass 188, four years; five years from July 2021) then permanent residence (888) if conditions are met; Australian citizenship can follow after the usual residence requirement for permanent residents. Streams over time: Business Innovation, Investor (AUD1.5m bonds 2012-2021; AUD2.5m complying investment 2021-2024), Significant Investor (see aus-siv), Premium Investor (2015-2021, AUD15m, not researched here), Entrepreneur, Business Talent, Venture Capital Entrepreneur. Most applicants needed state/territory nomination. Closed to new applications in July 2024 (1 July per the 2024-25 Migration Program report, 31 July per the visa website); on-hand applications still processed. Programme numbers are Migration Program places, primary and secondary applicants together.

name: Pre-2012 Business Skills investor visas: Investor (Provisional) subclass 162, State/Territory Sponsored Investor (Provisional) subclass 165, State/Territory Sponsored Business Investor (Residence) subclass 893
notes: Investor visas of the Business Skills programme (first version established in 1992, per a 2016 Home Affairs FOI release), replaced by the Business Innovation and Investment Program (aus-biip) from 1 July 2012; the provisional visas are closed to most new applications (family members can still be added). Applicants made a 'designated investment' (state or territory government bonds) for four years, then could apply for permanent residence (892/893). Investment thresholds over time not yet sourced. Only tail-end grants appear in the Migration Program data from 2015-16.

name: Premium Investor visa: Premium Investor stream of the Business Innovation and Investment visa (subclass 188 provisional, 888 permanent)
notes: By-invitation stream within aus-biip for people nominated by Austrade (no state nomination, no unsolicited expressions of interest) who made a complying premium investment of at least AUD15 million and held it for 12 months, after which they could apply for permanent residence (subclass 888 Premium Investor). Introduced 1 July 2015 alongside the revised Significant Investor rules; closed to new applications from 1 July 2021 after the BIIP review. Barely used: Home Affairs FOI releases show no applications or grants to 31 May 2017, fewer than five in 2018-19 and none from July 2019 to March 2020; the Migration Program data record a single primary grant (a Canadian national, 2018-19).

name: Significant Investor visa (SIV): Significant Investor stream of the Business Innovation and Investment visa (subclass 188C provisional, 888C permanent)
notes: A stream within aus-biip, kept as its own programme because it is the "golden visa" part. AUD5 million complying investment held for the provisional visa (four years; five from July 2021), with Complying Investment Framework rules from 1 July 2015 and revised ratios from 1 July 2021. No points test; nomination by a state/territory government or Austrade. For permanent residence (888) the investor had to spend 40 days a year in Australia, or the spouse 180 days. Permanent residents can later apply for citizenship under the normal residence rules. 2,264 primary SIVs were granted to 31 Oct 2019; most applicants were Chinese nationals. Closed to new applications 31 July 2024.

name: Austrian citizenship in the special interest of the Republic (Staatsbürgerschaftsgesetz 1985, § 10 Abs. 6, 'außerordentliche Leistungen')
notes: Not an advertised investment programme and no published price. A constitutional provision lets a Land grant citizenship without 10 years' residence, proof of income or renunciation of the old nationality when the federal government confirms that the person's past and expected 'extraordinary achievements' are in the special interest of the Republic. Used for scientists, artists, athletes and business people alike; official statistics do not split by field. Procedure regulated by BGBl. II 39/2014. Names and professions of confirmed persons are published (at least since 2016-2017). Statistik Austria counts 10 to 54 naturalisations a year in 2007-2023. The European Commission (COM(2019) 12, p. 4, fn. 10) lists Austria among states whose law equates national interest with economic interest. The 1965 start date comes from a ministry statement (8483/AB).

name: Bulgarian citizenship by investment (Закон за българското гражданство, art. 12a ordinary route and art. 14a fast-track route)
notes: Naturalisation for holders of investor permanent residence. Art. 12a (ordinary): after 5 years of permanent residence, investment of about EUR 500,000 (BGN 1 million). Art. 14a (fast track, added Feb 2013): after 1 year, investment increased to about EUR 1 million (BGN 2 million) or a priority-project route; no language test or real residence needed. Both repealed by the law in State Gazette no. 26 of 1 Apr 2022; pending procedures were ended and SANS was told to review past naturalisations. Ministry of Justice: 50 investor citizenships 2013-Jan 2019 (4 art. 12a, 46 art. 14a). launched=2005 is the year the Commission gives for the scheme's introduction; the fast track dates from 2013.

name: Bulgaria permanent residence for investors (Закон за чужденците в Република България, art. 25(1) items 6-8)
notes: Permanent (not temporary) residence permit for foreigners who invest, e.g. BGN 1 million in concession rights, collective investment schemes or alternative investment funds, BGN 2 million in listed shares or in a certified priority project, or BGN 6 million in an unlisted company (amounts as in the consolidated law on 2 Oct 2026). It was the first step to citizenship under arts. 12a/14a until 2022 and still exists. Ordinary naturalisation after 5 years of permanent residence remains possible under the general rules (language test etc.). Launch year not established; investor items date from 2005/2009 amendments. The Bulgarian Investment Agency certifies the investments: 981 persons certified 2014-Aug 2021 (both stages).

name: Golden Residency (الإقامة الذهبية)
notes: 10-year renewable residence permit created by Minister of Interior Order No. 20 of 2022 (dated 10 Feb 2022; launched 7 Feb 2022). Categories: owners of property in Bahrain worth at least BHD 200,000 at purchase (cut to BHD 130,000 in November 2025), retirees with BHD 4,000 a month pension, long-serving employees (5 years, BHD 2,000 average salary) and retirees (15 years, BHD 2,000), and talents. Fee BHD 300 per person per 10-year permit (plus BHD 5 application fee now). Holder must be present at least 90 days a year. The property route is the only investment route. A separate 'platinum' residence (PM Resolution 47/2023) is for long-serving golden holders. No path to citizenship is stated. Official counts are press statements covering all categories together.

name: Bahamas Economic Permanent Residence (economic permanent residence certificate, s.17A Immigration Act Ch. 191)
notes: Before July 2021, investors applied for ordinary permanent residence under the Immigration Act with administrative "accelerated consideration" for home buyers (US$500,000, raised to US$1.5m in 2011; a $750,000 real estate threshold applied by 2019-2021). Section 17A (in force 1 July 2021) made it statutory: a home and/or investment of a ministerially prescribed amount, 90 days' residence a year, investment kept 10 years. From 1 January 2025: $1 million in real estate or Central Bank zero coupon bonds for 10 years. Certificates are for life; right to work only in own business. Fees $25,000 (with right to work) or $20,000. Permanent residence does not lead to citizenship automatically. No official count of economic PR grants was found. Listed by the OECD in 2018 as potentially high-risk for CRS avoidance.

name: Belize economic citizenship programme
notes: Citizenship sold to 'economic citizens' under the Belize Nationality Act; the Act still mentions dependants of an 'economic citizen'. The US State Department listed Belize as selling economic citizenship in 2000 and 2001, at $25,000 per person (currency not stated), and reported that Belize announced it would stop in January 2002 after two buyers linked to a terrorist group were refused US visas. Start date, legal text and numbers sold not found.

name: Economic Investment Residential Certificate (EIRC; Economic Investment Certificate and Residential Certificate policy until 31 March 2023)
notes: Ministerial policy under s.32(5) of the Bermuda Immigration and Protection Act 1956, not a separate statute. Investment of at least BD$2.5 million (real estate, new or existing business, charity, Sinking Fund, Trust Fund, other approved ventures; Government bonds until 9 June 2024). From 2021 to March 2023 investors first got a five-year Economic Investment Certificate, then could apply for a Residential Certificate; since 31 March 2023 the Residential Certificate (indefinite residence, automatic work approval for the investor's own business) is granted at once, subject to keeping the investment and spending 90 days a year in Bermuda for five years. Replaced the 2003 and 2015 Residential Certificate policies for wealthy retirees. Not a route to Bermudian status or citizenship by itself. Cumulative figures from the Ministry: 79 approved applications, 188 holders and $604.9m associated investment by 5 November 2025.

name: Brazil residence authorisation for investors (autorização de residência para investidor: Resolução Normativa CNIg 13/2017, business; RN 36/2018 as replaced by RN 46, real estate)
notes: Two routes under the 2017 Migration Law (Lei 13.445) and Decreto 9.199/2017, set by resolutions of the National Immigration Council (CNIg): investment of own foreign funds in a Brazilian company (R$150,000 under RN 84/2009; R$500,000 from RN 118/2015, kept by RN 13/2017) and purchase of urban residential property with foreign funds (RN 36/2018: R$1,000,000, R$700,000 in the North and Northeast; replaced by RN 46, which kept the amounts and per the Agência Gov release gives an initial authorisation of up to four years, renewable). Granted by the Ministry of Justice (CGIL). 252 business and 290 real-estate authorisations in 2025. Naturalisation follows general rules. Launch shown as 2009 (RN 84); earlier investor rules were not checked.

name: Barbados Special Entry and Reside Permit (SERP)
notes: Long-term or indefinite residence permit granted by varying permission to stay under s.13(3) of the Immigration Act, Cap. 190. According to practitioner sources (not confirmed officially): Category 1 for investors of US$2m with net worth over US$5m (with work permit eligibility); Category 2 for owners of US$300,000 of real estate (5-year renewable, indefinite from age 60). Launch date and legal instrument not found. Listed by the OECD in 2018 as potentially high-risk for CRS avoidance. No counts found.

name: Canada federal Immigrant Investor Program (Investor class, Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations ss. 88-109)
notes: Permanent residence (no conditions after arrival) for experienced business people who lent the federal government a fixed sum for five years without interest; the money was passed to participating provinces and territories and repaid. C$400,000 loan and C$800,000 net worth until 30 Nov 2010, then C$800,000 and C$1.6 million. Introduced 1986, redesigned 1 April 1999. Cap of 700 new applications a year from 1 July 2011; intake stopped 1 July 2012. Budget 2014 (11 Feb 2014) announced its end; section 87.5 IRPA (Economic Action Plan 2014 Act, No. 1, assent 19 June 2014) terminated every application not assessed before 11 Feb 2014 and ordered refunds (it did not apply to investors selected by Quebec). Ordinary naturalisation rules apply afterwards (no investor-specific route). The 2014 CIC evaluation found investor immigrants declared low incomes and paid little income tax, had the highest out-migration after 10 years, and that only about 30% of the loan money was actively invested.

name: Canada Immigrant Investor Venture Capital (IIVC) pilot (Immigrant Investor Venture Capital class, ministerial instructions under IRPA s. 14.1)
notes: Replacement pilot for the federal IIP: permanent residence for up to 60 investors with net worth of at least C$10 million who paid C$2 million, not guaranteed, into a venture capital fund (held about 15 years and managed mainly by BDC Capital, per CBC), plus language and education requirements and a due diligence report. Intake windows 28 Jan-11 Feb 2015 (max 500 applications), 13 Feb-15 Apr 2015 and 25 May-30 Dec 2015. IRCC told CBC only seven applications were in process when intake closed on 30 Dec 2015. IRCC declared the pilot closed and removed its instructions on 29 Jan 2021 after finalising the last files. Final admissions not found.

name: Quebec Investor Program (Programme des investisseurs, Règlement sur l'immigration au Québec, art. 37 and following)
notes: Quebec selects the investor (selection certificate, CSQ) under the Canada-Quebec Accord; IRCC then grants permanent residence. Investors place a fixed sum for 5 years with IQ Immigrants Investisseurs (a subsidiary of Investissement Québec) through an authorised broker or trust company; the income funds grants to Quebec businesses. Placement of C$1,200,000 (net worth C$2 million) under the regulation in force from 2 August 2018 (the amount before then was not confirmed in a Quebec text in this pass); from 1 January 2024 a C$1,000,000 placement plus a non-refundable C$200,000 contribution, oral French level 7, a work permit and stays of at least 6 months each for the investor and spouse in Quebec (no stay required before). Receipt of applications was suspended 1 Apr-15 Aug 2018; capped at 1,900 (max 1,235 from China) for 10 Sep 2018-31 Aug 2019; suspended again 1 Nov 2019 to 1 Apr 2023. Under the new rules only C$1 million (2024-25) and C$3 million (Apr-Dec 2025) of placements were made. MIFI found only 15.5% of people admitted 2011-2020 still present in Quebec in January 2022. Launch year of the Quebec programme is not stated in the sources read (the federal investor class dates from 1986).

name: Besteuerung nach dem Aufwand / imposition d'après la dépense (Swiss lump-sum taxation)
notes: Not a residence permit but a tax regime (art. 14 DBG and cantonal law) for foreign nationals who take up residence in Switzerland for the first time (or after 10 years away) and do not work there: tax is assessed on worldwide living expenses, with a federal minimum base of CHF 400,000 from 2016 (indexed: CHF 421,700, then CHF 435,000 from 2026) and at least seven times the rent. Abolished in five cantons (ZH, BS, BL, SH, AR); a national abolition initiative failed in 2014. Non-EU nationals need a cantonal permit (che-wealthy-residence-permit). FDK surveys give taxpayer numbers and revenue to 2018. Launch date of this very old regime not established.

name: Aufenthaltsbewilligung wegen erheblicher kantonaler fiskalischer Interessen (Swiss residence permit for wealthy non-working foreigners, art. 30 para. 1(b) AIG / art. 32 VZAE)
notes: Cantons may grant a short-stay or residence permit to protect important public interests, including substantial cantonal fiscal interests (art. 32(1)(c) VZAE); used for wealthy non-EU/EFTA nationals who do not work in Switzerland, typically combined with lump-sum taxation. Each canton sets its own minimum tax expectation; no federal amounts. No official statistics on permits granted on this ground were found.

name: Comoros economic citizenship programme (citoyenneté économique)
notes: Law on economic citizenship signed by President Sambi on 27 Nov 2008 after an earlier rejection (July 2008); a parliamentary inquiry later found the vote broke procedure. Mainly bulk sales to the UAE (and talks with Kuwait) to document stateless Bidoon, who did not move to Comoros; an initial deal of $200m for 4,000 families, then (2011) EUR 4,600 per passport with a minimum of 5,000. The IMF describes it as citizenship for KMF 1 million (about US$3,000) per person, with receipts routed via the Banque de France. Proceeds were large relative to GDP (IMF: about 3-4.5% in 2012 in 2013 reports, over 6% in the 2015 report). Passports were also sold outside the official channel, including to Iranians. Suspended after President Azali took office in May 2016. A parliamentary commission (set up June 2017, report Dec 2017) estimated missing revenue of $100m (Reuters) or $971m (AFP); the State Security Court sentenced ex-president Sambi to life for 'high treason' on 28 Nov 2022. Official law text and commission report not obtained.

name: Costa Rica temporary residence as investor (residencia temporal, categoría inversionista: Ley General de Migración y Extranjería 8764 art. 79; Reglamento de Extranjería arts. 87-93; Ley 9996)
notes: Temporary residence for a foreigner who invests at least US$200,000 (Reglamento de Extranjería 2012, art. 87) in real estate, registrable goods, shares, securities, productive projects or projects of national interest; Ley 9996 (in force 14 July 2021) set a new minimum of US$150,000 "for the period set by this law", added venture capital funds and sustainable tourism projects, and gave tax and import exemptions that could be claimed only in the first five years (to July 2026). Whether the US$150,000 threshold continues after July 2026 is unclear from the law's wording; not resolved in this pass. Run by the Dirección General de Migración y Extranjería (DGME). No official counts found. Launch date of the investor category before the 2012 regulation not checked.

name: Cayman Islands Certificate of Direct Investment
notes: Section 47 of the Immigration (Transition) Act (s.37A of the former Law). Investment of at least CI$1m in a licensed employment-generating business in which the holder has substantial management control; 25-year certificate with right to work in that business; audited accounts and job details at years 2 and 5. Issue fee CI$20,000 (draft 2026: CI$50,000). Launch date not established. No counts found.

name: Cayman Islands Certificate of Permanent Residence for Persons of Independent Means
notes: Created by the Immigration (Amendment) Law 2012 (s.34A, now s.42 of the Immigration (Transition) Act). Requires investment in developed real estate: CI$1.6m, CI$2m since May 2017. Issue fee CI$100,000 (draft 2026: CI$200,000); quota 250 a year. No right to work unless varied by the Board. From 1 May 2026 the certificate is for 10 years, renewable indefinitely, and the holder may then apply for naturalisation as a British Overseas Territories citizen (residence rules of the British Nationality Act still apply). No official counts found.

name: Cayman Islands Residency Certificate for Persons of Independent Means (25-year)
notes: Section 41 of the Immigration (Transition) Act (s.34 of the former Immigration Law). 25-year certificate, renewable, without the right to work. Since May 2017: CI$1m invested of which CI$500,000 in developed real estate on Grand Cayman (half on the Sister Islands), plus CI$120,000 annual income or a CI$400,000 local deposit; holders must be present 30 days a year. Issue fee CI$20,000 (draft 2026: CI$50,000). Launch date not established (predates the 2014 revision; the Act refers to a separate retirees' certificate under the 2003 Law). No official counts found.

name: Cayman Islands Residency Certificate (Substantial Business Presence)
notes: Created by the Immigration (Amendment) Law 2012 (s.37D, now s.50). For owners or senior managers of an approved category of business (fund administration, insurance, family office, exempted companies etc.) with physical premises and at least four full-time resident staff; no fixed investment amount. Issue fee CI$5,000 (draft 2026: CI$12,500). No counts found.

name: Cyprus Investment Programme (Κυπριακό Επενδυτικό Πρόγραμμα, ΚΕΠ), incl. the 2007-2013 scheme for exceptional naturalisation of foreign investors
notes: Naturalisation by Council of Ministers decision, without residence: 2007-2013 under para 2(στ) of the Third Schedule of the Civil Registry Law (exceptional services), from 30 Apr 2013 under art. 111A(2) (Law 36(I)/2013), from 18 Aug 2020 under regulations ΚΔΠ 379/2020. Criteria changed 12 times by Council decisions. Abolished by decision of 13 Oct 2020: no applications after 31 Oct 2020; pending ones approved until 31 Jul 2021. 6,779 naturalisations to 17 Aug 2020 (inquiry); 3,517 investors and 3,810 family members to 31 Jul 2021 (Audit Office). Art. 111A(2) deleted by a law passed in late 2025 or early 2026; EU infringement closed 11 Mar 2026.

name: Cyprus fast-track permanent residence for investors (Άδεια Μετανάστευσης, Regulation 6(2) of the Aliens and Immigration Regulations; 'golden visa')
notes: Permanent residence (Immigration Permit) for third-country investors, issued by the Minister of Interior under Regulation 6(2); EUR 300,000 investment plus EUR 50,000 annual income (2023 criteria). No right to work except as director of the invested company. Card valid 10 years; right of residence unlimited. It does not lead to citizenship by itself; naturalisation needs years of actual residence under the ordinary rules (not researched here). Launch date and pre-2021 terms not verified. No official numbers of permits found.

name: Commonwealth of Dominica Citizenship by Investment Programme
notes: Originally the Economic Citizenship Programme (ECP); administered by the Citizenship by Investment Unit (CBIU). Routes: Economic Diversification Fund contribution and approved real estate. Under EU request (June 2026) to phase out by 1 June 2028.

name: Dominican Republic residence by investment (residencia por inversión)
notes: Investor residence processed by the Dirección General de Migración on the basis of an investment certified by ProDominicana; integrated into the single investment window in 2024. Legal basis believed to be the General Migration Law 285-04 and its Regulation (Decree 631-11), with Law 171-07 for pensioners and rentiers, but the provisions were not read. Minimum amount not confirmed: the Migration director cited US$250,000 in 2021; advisers commonly cite US$200,000. No counts found.

name: Egyptian citizenship through investment programmes (الجنسية المصرية بالبرامج الاستثمارية; Nationality Law 26/1975 Art. 4 bis)
notes: Naturalisation by Prime Minister's decree on the recommendation of a Cabinet unit (members from Foreign Affairs, Interior, Investment/International Cooperation and security agencies), under Art. 4 bis of the Nationality Law as replaced by Law 140/2019 (30 Jul 2019). Routes and amounts set by PM Decree 3099/2019 (Dec 2019; text not obtained), amended by PM Decrees 876/2023 (in force 3 Mar 2023) and 3562/2023 (19 Sep 2023); the unit was organised by PM Decree 647/2020. Current routes: property USD 300,000; investment project USD 350,000 plus USD 100,000 to the Treasury; USD 500,000 deposit at the Central Bank refunded in EGP after 3 years without interest; USD 250,000 non-refundable payment. USD 10,000 application fee. Selling the property or project within 5 years requires a USD 250,000 payment to keep citizenship. No residence requirement. Each grant is published as a named PM decree in the Official Gazette; no aggregate statistics are published. The 'launched' date is the decree month; applications reportedly opened in 2020.

name: Egypt 'deposit residence' (إقامة بوديعة) for foreign investors, Law 173/2018
notes: Created by Law 173/2018 (Gazette 14 Aug 2018, in force the next day): residence category for foreigners depositing at least EGP 7 million (or foreign-currency equivalent) in an Egyptian bank; after five consecutive years the Interior Minister could naturalise them, the deposit then passing to the Treasury. Implementing rules were to be set by an Interior Minister decree. Repealed by Law 140/2019 (30 Jul 2019), which replaced it with the egy-cbi programme. No evidence found that any permit was issued; 'ended' is the month of the repealing law (Gazette publication date not verified).

name: Spain investor visa and residence authorisation (visado y autorización de residencia para inversores, Ley 14/2013, 'golden visa')
notes: Residence (not citizenship) for non-EU investors under arts. 61-67 of Ley 14/2013 (in force 29 Sep 2013). Routes: EUR 500,000 real estate per applicant; EUR 2m Spanish public debt; EUR 1m in shares of Spanish companies or in Spanish bank deposits; from 30 Jul 2015 also EUR 1m in Spanish investment/venture-capital funds; business project of general interest (no fixed amount). Visas issued by consulates (Foreign Ministry); residence authorisations granted in Spain by the Directorate-General for Migration and processed by the Unidad de Grandes Empresas y Colectivos Estratégicos (UGE-CE). Visa 1 year; initial authorisation 2 years (3 years from 23 Dec 2022); renewals 2 years, then 5 years from 30 Jul 2015. Family members got derivative permits. The law gave no shortcut to citizenship. Arts. 63-67 emptied by Ley Orgánica 1/2025 (in force 3 Apr 2025); existing permits may be renewed. Official statistics are scattered: one 2015 ministry report, parliamentary answers, and 2024 press releases whose counts do not match each other (consular visas vs all authorisations).

name: Elamisluba ettevõtluseks, sh suurinvestorile (Estonian temporary residence permit for enterprise, including for large investors)
notes: Aliens Act: temporary residence permit for enterprise (EUR 65,000 invested in a company, or EUR 16,000 for a sole proprietor) and, from 18 Jan 2017, for large investors (EUR 1,000,000 directly invested in an Estonian company or fund, no obligation to live in Estonia). Permits up to 5 years, renewable. The Commission dates the Estonian investor scheme to 2009. Three large-investor permits were issued in 2017 (all to Russians). No official series found for later years.

name: Passeport talent - investisseur économique (French Tech Visa for investors)
notes: Multi-year residence card (up to 4 years) for a foreigner who invests at least EUR 300,000 in France, personally or through a company he runs or owns at least 30% of, creating or saving jobs within four years. Part of the passeport talent created by the law of 7 Mar 2016 (the Commission dates the French scheme to 2016). The Commission reported 29 permits in 2017; no later official breakdown was found.

name: Tier 1 (Investor) visa (United Kingdom)
notes: Residence by investment under Part 6A of the Immigration Rules (paras 245E-245EF; originally 245O-245U), created by HC 607 from 30 June 2008, replacing an 'investor' category that had existed since 1 October 1994. Investors held GBP 1m (GBP 2m from 6 Nov 2014) and invested it in UK government bonds (until 29 March 2019) or share/loan capital of UK trading companies; no job or business required. First grant 3 years 4 months, extension 2 years. Settlement (indefinite leave to remain) after 5 years, or after 3 years with GBP 5m / 2 years with GBP 10m (from 6 April 2011). Citizenship by naturalisation possible 12 months after settlement and 5 years' residence (MAC 2014: 6 years at GBP 1m, 5 years at GBP 5m/10m). Closed to new applicants at 16:00 on 17 Feb 2022 by CP 632; existing investors could extend until 17 Feb 2026 and may apply to settle until 17 Feb 2028. Home Office statistics count visas per person and separate main applicants from dependants; no official figure for total money invested.

name: Greece Golden Visa (Μόνιμη άδεια διαμονής επενδυτή - permanent investor residence permit, real estate)
notes: Residence (not citizenship): five-year renewable permit, no right to work, no minimum stay; family members get derivative permits. Legal basis: art. 36A Law 3386/2005 (added by Law 4146/2013) -> art. 20(B) Law 4251/2014 -> art. 100 Law 5038/2023 (type B.5). Financial-investment permits (art. 16 Law 4251/2014 / art. 99 Law 5038/2023, type B.4) are a separate permit type. Ministry statistics count permits (one per person) and distinguish main investors vs family members and first grant vs renewal.

name: Grenada Citizenship by Investment Programme (Investment Migration Agency Grenada)
notes: Legal basis: Grenada Citizenship by Investment Act No. 15 of 2013 and SRO 17 of 2013. First approvals 2014. Routes: NTF donation, approved real estate, significant investment (from 2024 statistics). Unit rebranded IMA in March 2024.

name: Grenada Economic Citizenship Program (1997-2001)
notes: Predecessor scheme; suspended indefinitely after 9/11 (UNGA statement Nov 2001). Details only from secondary/industry sources. Proposed as a separate program_id; merge into grd-cbi if the dataset prefers one id per jurisdiction.

name: Capital Investment Entrant Scheme (CIES; 資本投資者入境計劃)
notes: Residence (not citizenship) for people who invest in Hong Kong without running a business there; run by the Immigration Department under the 'Rules for the Capital Investment Entrant Scheme' (ID(E)968); no law establishing it was found. Threshold HK$6.5m in property and/or financial assets from 27 Oct 2003; HK$10m in financial assets only from 14 Oct 2010. Open to foreign nationals, Macao and Taiwan residents, stateless persons and Chinese nationals holding permanent residence abroad (not Mainland residents). Two steps: approval-in-principle (enter as a visitor to invest within six months), then formal approval and two-year permissions to stay, renewed if the investment is kept. After seven years' continuous ordinary residence investors and dependants could apply for the right of abode (permanent residence) under the Basic Law. Suspended 'until further notice' from 15 Jan 2015; applications already received were still processed and all were finalised in October 2023. The large majority of applicants were Chinese nationals with foreign permanent residence; of those formally approved to end-2007, the largest groups held permanent residence in Gambia (414 of 1,114), Canada, New Zealand, Nauru, Australia, the Philippines, Niger and Guinea-Bissau (LCQ12, 2008).

name: New Capital Investment Entrant Scheme (New CIES; 新資本投資者入境計劃)
notes: Residence for investors of at least HK$30m: HK$27m in permissible financial assets and/or real estate (real estate counts for at most HK$10m; residential only for single properties of HK$50m+ from 16 Oct 2024) plus HK$3m in the CIES Investment Portfolio managed by the Hong Kong Investment Corporation. Approved by the Executive Council on 19 Dec 2023; no law establishing it was found. InvestHK verifies net assets (HK$30m, held two years before applying until Feb 2025, six months from 1 Mar 2025) and the investment; ImmD grants approval-in-principle (180-day visitor stay to invest), then formal approval: 2 years' stay, then 3-year extensions. After seven years' continuous ordinary residence applicants and dependants may apply for permanent residence; those who keep the investment seven years without meeting the residence test may apply for unconditional stay. Eligible: foreign nationals (except Afghanistan, Cuba, North Korea), Chinese nationals with foreign permanent residence, Macao residents, Chinese residents of Taiwan. Official figures are cumulative press-release totals; the only country breakdowns found (May 2024, March 2025) are led by Guinea-Bissau and Vanuatu.

name: Dozvola za boravak i rad za samozapošljavanje (Croatian residence and work permit for self-employed company owners, Zakon o strancima art. 113)
notes: Not a passive investor visa: residence and work permit for a third-country national who owns at least 51% of a company or craft, invested at least EUR 26,544.56 and employs at least three Croatian citizens full-time; key staff of companies with the same capital may also qualify; separate permit for strategic investment projects (art. 115). The Commission (2019) lists Croatia among states with an investor residence scheme (since 2011) and found no statistics. No counts found.

name: Hungarian Guest Investor Program (vendégbefektetői vízum és tartózkodási engedély)
notes: Act XC of 2023, ss. 16 and 22: six-month guest investor visa, then a 10-year residence permit renewable for 10 more, with the right to work. Routes: EUR 250,000 in units of a qualified Hungarian real estate fund held 5 years; EUR 1,000,000 donation to a foundation-run university; EUR 500,000 residential property until removed on 30 Dec 2024. Security vetting by the Constitution Protection Office; fund managers need clearance. Law in force 1 Jan 2024, but the first fund manager qualified only in Oct 2024. No official statistics are published; press reports from OIF data show very low take-up.

name: Hungarian residency bond programme (Letelepedési Magyar Államkötvény, settlement bond)
notes: Residence permit in the 'national economic interest' under s. 28(3)-(11) of Act II of 2007 (added by Act CCXX of 2012) for holders of at least EUR 250,000 (EUR 300,000 from 2015) of five-year securities sold by private intermediaries approved by Parliament's economic committee (eight in all, mostly offshore; one per country); the intermediaries bought discounted zero-coupon euro bonds from ÁKK. Settlement (permanent residence) permit after six months, directly from July 2016 per Index. ÁKK: EUR 1.844 billion face value issued 2013-2017 in 11 series, all repaid by 2022. BMH: about 6,500 investors and 13,300 family members. Residence route only; normal naturalisation rules applied.

name: Golden Visa Indonesia
notes: Five- or ten-year limited-stay permit (renewable) run by the Directorate General of Immigration, launched 25 July 2024, for corporate investors, individual investors (with or without founding a company), global talent, 'second home', 'silver hair' retirees, world figures, former Indonesians and descendants, and investors in the new capital (IKN). Individual investors who do not found a company place US$350,000 (5 years) or US$700,000 (10 years) in Indonesian government bonds, listed shares or deposits; those founding a company invest US$2.5m/US$5m; corporate directors US$25m/US$50m. No guarantor needed. The implementing regulation (a Minister of Law and Human Rights regulation on visas and stay permits, 2023-2024) could not be downloaded and is not cited. Separate from the Global Citizen of Indonesia (GCI) permit of January 2026 for diaspora.

name: Investment-based naturalisation scheme ('passports for investment')
notes: No law of its own: the Minister for Justice used the discretion in section 16 of the Irish Nationality and Citizenship Act 1956 (as amended 1986) to waive the residence condition for investors, treating the investment as 'Irish associations'. Government approved the approach in April 1989, but the Department's review counts naturalisations from 1988 (and the 2002 Minister said it was introduced in 1988; the 2000 Minister said 1989). Applicant, spouse and children under 18 could be included. Before 1994 the Department's working rule was about IR£500,000; from October 1994 an advisory group applied a minimum net investment of IR£1 million per applicant, a residence to be kept 5 years and 60 days' presence in the 2 years after naturalisation. New applications stopped on 4 Sep 1996; the scheme was formally ended on 20 Apr 1998, but cases already accepted were processed later (naturalisations recorded up to 2004). Section 10 of the Irish Nationality and Citizenship Act 2004 removed the legal basis. Totals given to the Dáil: 143 persons by Feb 1998; 183 persons (107 investors) in the final count. The Department's 1998 review found most early cases did not meet the published conditions (e.g. good-character evidence in 17 of 66).

name: Immigrant Investor Programme (IIP)
notes: Residence by investment run by the Department of Justice (INIS, later Immigration Service Delivery) under a Government decision of 2012 and ministerial guidelines, without its own legislation. Approved investors and their spouse/partner and minor children got Stamp 4 residence (right to work and study): 2 years, renewed for 3, then 5-year renewals while the investment (held at least 3 years) stayed in place. No residence obligation beyond visiting Ireland once a year. No fast track to citizenship: naturalisation needs 5 years' physical (reckonable) residence, so investors who did not live in Ireland could not qualify. Projects were vetted by an inter-departmental Evaluation Committee; the minister decided. Most money went via the enterprise option into project vehicles (nursing homes, social housing, hotels) put together by agents for groups of mainly Chinese investors. Closed to new applications 15 Feb 2023; applications on hand and investors for already approved projects are still being processed (1,192 pending in March 2026).

name: Investor Visa for Italy (visto per investitori, art. 26-bis D.Lgs. 286/1998)
notes: Entry visa and two-year 'per investitori' residence permit, renewable for three years at a time, for non-EU nationals who invest EUR 2m in Italian government bonds, EUR 500k (EUR 1m until 18 May 2020) in an Italian company (from 18 Dec 2024 also an Italian venture-capital fund), EUR 250k (EUR 500k until 18 May 2020) in an innovative start-up, or donate EUR 1m to a public-interest project; investment must be made within 3 months of arrival and held for 2 years. Legal basis in force 1 Jan 2017 (L. 232/2016, art. 1, c. 148); implementing decree 21 Jul 2017; applications run through an online portal from 14 Dec 2017, vetted by an inter-ministerial Committee chaired by the ministry of enterprise (MISE, now MIMIT), which issues a nulla osta. No real-estate route. Applications free of charge. Holders may apply for an EU long-term permit after 5 years of holding the investment (portal); no special route to citizenship. Suspended for Russian and Belarusian citizens from 14 Jul 2023 and for dual nationals with a Russian or Belarusian passport from 20 Mar 2024. Very low uptake: 13 applications to end-2019 (latest official total found).

name: Jordanian citizenship for investors (أسس منح المستثمرين الجنسية الأردنية)
notes: Not a statute: Cabinet decisions setting 'bases' for naturalising investors (Nationality Law allows Cabinet discretion). Rules changed in Dec 2019 (amounts cut), 12 Sep 2021 (decision 3657: deposit+bonds, shares, new and existing projects; 500 investors a year cap), 2022 (decision 6404: sector routes; employment route), and 2 Jul 2025 (decision 4375: amounts in JOD, deposit/bond route dropped). New-project investors first get a 3-year temporary passport (no political rights) and citizenship after 3 years of compliance. Applications go to the Ministry of Investment (earlier the Jordan Investment Commission); a special investors committee chaired by the Interior Minister (decision 5995 of 19 Aug 2019) recommends to the Cabinet; security approval is required. Launch year 2018 is reported (JIC/Jordan Times give the 'previous' amounts); the 2018 decision itself was not obtained.

name: Jordan five-year residence for property buyers (الإقامة لمدة خمس سنوات عن طريق شراء عقار)
notes: Five-year renewable residence for investors or ordinary persons buying one or more residential properties worth at least JOD 200,000 (Department of Lands and Survey valuation), held 5 years without sale or mortgage; issued by the Interior Minister on the investor committee's recommendation; spouse and children included. Since decision 4375 (2025) the purchase must be new and from a licensed developer. Residence does not lead to citizenship by itself (ordinary naturalisation rules apply). Earliest official evidence found: JIC sheet of Jan 2021; launch date not established.

name: Cambodia: naturalisation by investment or donation (Law on Nationality 1996, Arts 10-12; Law on Nationality 2018, Arts 21-22; Sub-decree No. 225 of 2025)
notes: Under the 1996 law, investors spending 1,250,000,000 riels were exempted from the 7-year residence requirement and donors of 1,000,000,000 riels to the national budget could apply; granted by Royal Decree, with an optional Khmer name. The 2018 law moved the amounts into a sub-decree (No. 112 of 30 Aug 2018, not found) and added 12 months' (investors) or 6 months' (donors) legal residence. Sub-decree No. 225 of 1 Dec 2025 sets 4,000,000,000 riel (investment in priority sectors) and 12,000,000,000 riel (donation). Naturalisations were published in the Royal Gazette until February 2024 (about 50 a month in 2020-2023, all routes); no official count by route. Several naturalised China-born businessmen were later sanctioned or prosecuted abroad.

name: St. Kitts and Nevis Citizenship by Investment Programme
notes: Oldest CBI program. Routes over time: SIDF donation (from 2006), Hurricane Relief Fund (c. 2017-2018), Sustainable Growth Fund (to July 2023), Sustainable Island State Contribution (from 27 July 2023), approved real estate, private homes, public benefit option, alternative investment options (2020-2023). CIU became a statutory body in 2024.

name: Public-project investment immigration (공익사업 투자이민제)
notes: Foreigners who place money in a public-interest fund run by the Korea Development Bank (principal returned without interest after five years, lent to small firms) or in designated development projects get F-2 residence and, after five years, F-5 permanent residence; the high-value scheme gives F-5 immediately on a pledge to keep the investment five years. General scheme 500m won (from May 2013), retirement scheme 300m won for 55+ (May 2013, abolished 29 June 2023), high-value 1.5bn won (Oct 2014). From 29 June 2023: 1.5bn and 3bn won.

name: Real-estate investment immigration (부동산 투자이민제), renamed tourism and resort facility investment immigration (관광·휴양시설 투자이민제) in 2023
notes: Foreigners who buy tourism or resort property above a threshold in areas designated by the Minister of Justice (Jeju, Incheon Songdo/Yeongjong/Cheongna, Busan Haeundae/East Busan, Pyeongchang Alpensia, Yeosu Gyeongdo) get a residence (F-2) visa and, after keeping the investment five years, permanent residence (F-5). Legal basis: Immigration Act Enforcement Decree (F-2/F-5 status) and Ministry of Justice notices; in Jeju also the Jeju Special Act art. 147. Threshold in Jeju 500 million won from 2010, 1 billion won everywhere from 1 May 2023, when investment was limited to resort condominiums, lodging and tourist pensions in tourism zones. Permanent residence leads to local voting rights, which drove the 2023 tightening. Overwhelmingly used by Chinese nationals.

name: Saint Lucia Citizenship by Investment Programme (CIP Saint Lucia)
notes: Act No. 14 of 2015; regulations SI 89 of 2015 (2 Oct 2015); CIU operating from Oct 2015; first applications 1 Jan 2016. Fiscal year April-March.

name: Leidimas laikinai gyventi užsieniečiui, investavusiam į įmonę (Lithuanian temporary residence for company investors, Law on the Legal Status of Aliens art. 45(1)(1), (1¹), (2²))
notes: Temporary residence for a foreign participant or manager of a Lithuanian company: EUR 14,000 own investment in a company with at least EUR 28,000 equity and wage conditions, or EUR 260,000 investment with at least five jobs (added 2016), or managing a company with EUR 500,000 equity and ten jobs. The Commission (2019) dates Lithuania's scheme to 2004 and found no disaggregated statistics. No official counts found. Ordinary naturalisation requires 10 years of residence.

name: Autorisation de séjour pour investisseur (Luxembourg investor residence permit, arts. 53bis-53quater of the immigration law)
notes: Added by the law of 8 March 2017: residence for investing EUR 500,000 in an existing or new Luxembourg company, EUR 3 million in an investment and management structure, or EUR 20 million as a deposit with a Luxembourg financial institution; three-year title after a favourable opinion from the Economy or Finance ministry. Only 9 titles issued (2018-2024), none of the first 7 renewed. Government bill 8586 (21 Jul 2025) would repeal it; still in committee in Sep 2026. status = active until the repeal is adopted.

name: Latvia temporary residence permits for investors (Imigrācijas likums, 23. panta pirmās daļas 28.-31. punkts)
notes: Five-year renewable temporary residence permits (termiņuzturēšanās atļauja, TUA) for investors and their spouses and minor children, under art. 23(1) points 28 (company capital), 29 (real estate), 30 (subordinated liabilities with a Latvian bank) and 31 (interest-free state securities, 2015 to May 2026) of the 2002 Immigration Law; added by the law of 22.04.2010, in force 1 Jul 2010. Run by the Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs (PMLP). Russian and Belarusian citizens excluded from 24 Sep 2022. The state-securities route was deleted from 20 May 2026; the property and bank routes ended when the new Immigration Law took effect on 15 Sep 2026, which keeps a two-year business-investment permit and adds an (not yet operational) EUR 150,000 state fund route, so the programme continues in reduced form. Under art. 24(1) point 7 of the 2002 law, a foreigner who has lived in Latvia continuously with a temporary residence permit for at least five years may request permanent residence (other conditions, such as language, apply; not detailed here). Citizenship rules not researched.

name: Carte de séjour de résident (Monaco residence card, including for persons of independent means)
notes: Ordonnance Souveraine 3.153 of 1964: a first-time resident card needs housing and either a work permit or proof of sufficient means (art. 6); ordinary 3-year and privileged 10-year cards follow. The law sets no amount; officials and media describe a EUR 500,000 deposit in a Monaco bank as the usual means test for those not working. Not an investment programme in the strict sense, and not specific to non-EU nationals. About 1,300 first-card applications a year (all applicants). launched = date of the ordinance in force.

name: Programul de dobândire a cetățeniei prin investiție (Citizenship by Investment Programme of the Republic of Moldova)
notes: Legal basis: art. 17(11)-(12) of Citizenship Law no. 1024/2000 as amended (bill registered Dec 2016) and Government Decision no. 786 of 4 Oct 2017 (regulation). Run with Henley & Partners as the government's exclusive private operator. Routes as reported in the press: a non-refundable contribution of at least EUR 100,000 to the Public Investment Fund for Sustainable Development, or an investment of EUR 250,000 in a strategic sector held 60 months. Cap of 5,000 main applicants (CJI). Launched Nov 2018; moratorium on new applications from summer 2019 (Law 107/2019), extended; Parliament abolished the scheme on 18 Jun 2020 with effect from 1 Sep 2020. 38 applications for 98 people; 20 applications (52 people) successful by mid-2021 (EC). The text of HG 786/2017 itself was not read (legis.md blocked).

name: North Macedonia: naturalisation for special economic interest (Закон за државјанството, член 11; Уредба за утврдување на критериумите за особен ... национален интерес)
notes: Art. 11 of the Law on Citizenship (since 1992; reworded 2004) allows naturalisation without residence where it is of special scientific, economic, cultural, sporting or other national interest; the Government decides. Criteria decree of 2005 (no amounts); EUR 400,000 direct investment plus 10 jobs from 20 Dec 2012; EUR 200,000 private investment fund route added 14 Dec 2019. The Ministries of Finance and Economy assess economic interest and the security agency vets. 121 economic-interest grants 2005-2022 (40 refusals); one or two a year since. The European Commission (Dec 2025) says the scheme must be abolished under the Visa Suspension Mechanism; a June 2026 draft law would remove fixed amounts but keep investment as a criterion. This row covers the economic-interest route; some observations give other Art. 11 grounds (sport, culture, science) via breakdown. 'launched' is the first criteria decree; the legal basis dates from 1992.

name: Global Residence Programme (GRP)
notes: Special tax status under the Income Tax Act (L.N. 167 of 2013, S.L. 123.148) for non-EU nationals who buy (EUR 275,000; EUR 220,000 south/Gozo) or rent (EUR 9,600/8,750 a year) property in Malta: 15% tax on foreign income remitted to Malta, minimum EUR 15,000 a year. A tax-residence scheme run by the Commissioner for Revenue rather than an immigration permit, but it lets holders reside in Malta. Succeeded the 2011 High Net Worth Individuals non-EU rules (mlt-hnwi-non-eu). From 1 Jan 2027 the Individual Tax Programme Rules (L.N. 195/2026) apply, with much higher thresholds; existing statuses and applications made by 31 Dec 2026 continue to 31 Dec 2031. No official numbers of beneficiaries or tax collected were found.

name: High Net Worth Individuals - Non-EU/EEA/Swiss Nationals Rules (special tax status)
notes: L.N. 403 of 2011 (S.L. 123.130), deemed in force 1 Jan 2011: 15% tax status for non-EU nationals buying property of at least EUR 400,000 or renting at EUR 20,000 a year, minimum tax EUR 25,000 plus EUR 5,000 per dependant. No applications after 30 Jun 2013 (L.N. 178 of 2013); holders could move to the GRP.

name: Individual Investor Programme of the Republic of Malta (IIP)
notes: Closed to new applications 31 Jul 2020. Pending applications were processed until 2024 (6 naturalisations in 2024). Cap of 1,800 main applicants; 1,555 were naturalised.

name: Maltese Citizenship by Naturalisation for Exceptional Services by Direct Investment (Granting of Citizenship for Exceptional Services, GCES)
notes: Found contrary to EU law by the CJEU on 29 Apr 2025 (C-181/23). Discontinued by Act XXI of 2025, whose transitional clause keeps applications filed before it under the old rules. The date new applications actually stopped (reportedly 29 Apr 2025) was not verified in a primary source.

name: Malta Permanent Residence Programme (MPRP)
notes: Successor to the Malta Residence and Visa Programme (MRVP). Run by Residency Malta Agency. No official application or approval statistics were found.

name: Malta Residence and Visa Programme (MRVP)
notes: Created by L.N. 288 of 2015 (S.L. 217.18): residence certificate entitling the holder to reside, settle or stay indefinitely in exchange for a EUR 30,000 contribution, a EUR 250,000 qualifying investment (government stocks) and a qualifying property (EUR 320,000/270,000 purchase or EUR 12,000/10,000 rent). Run by Identity Malta, from 2017 by the Malta Residence and Visa Agency (later Residency Malta Agency). Replaced by the MPRP on 29 Mar 2021; L.N. 122 of 2021 set deadlines for pending applications (end-2021 / 31 Mar 2022). Most applicants were Chinese nationals. ended = closure to new applications.

name: Posebni program ulaganja od posebnog značaja za privredni i ekonomski interes Crne Gore (Special Investment Programme of Special Importance for the Economic Interest of Montenegro; "economic citizenship")
notes: Created by Government decision of 22 Nov 2018 (Službeni list CG 79/2018); applications from 1 Jan 2019. Applicant pays EUR 100,000 into an escrow account for less developed municipalities and invests at least EUR 450,000 (Podgorica or coast) or EUR 250,000 (north/centre) in a government-listed development project (in practice condo-hotel units), plus fees of EUR 15,000 per applicant and EUR 10,000 per family member. From 31 Dec 2021 an extra EUR 100,000 to the Innovation Fund. Cap of 2,000 decisions. Applications only through licensed intermediary agents (Henley & Partners, Arton, Apex), with due-diligence agents. Originally to end 31 Dec 2021; extended on 30 Dec 2021 to 31 Dec 2022, then expired; pending applications still decided in 2026 (5 left on 1 Sep 2026). 1,113 applications filed nationally, 869 approved, 239 refused; the EC counts 556 main applicants with 1,281 family members. Over 70% of passports to 2022 went to Russian citizens (EC).

name: Mauritius Family Occupation Permit (USD 250,000 contribution to the COVID-19 Projects Development Fund)
notes: A 10-year residence and work permit for an applicant, spouse, dependants and household staff in return for a non-refundable USD 250,000 contribution to the COVID-19 Projects Development Fund (Immigration Act s. 9CA, inserted by the Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2021; Immigration Act 2022 s. 14). The criteria were restated in the Finance Act 2025 but are absent from the EDB Act First Schedule as consolidated to Act 13 of 2026, so the current status is unclear. No figures on permits issued or money raised were found.

name: Mauritius naturalisation with reduced residence for investors (Mauritius Citizenship Act s. 9(3))
notes: Not a citizenship-by-investment programme with a price: the Minister may, at discretion, accept 2 years' continuous residence instead of the normal requirement (12 months immediately before plus 5 of the previous 7 years) for a person who has invested at least MUR 3 million (1995) or USD 500,000 'or such other sum as may be prescribed' (1999). The 1995 Act replaced an earlier version of s. 9(3) whose terms were not read. Applicants had to renounce other nationalities (s. 9(4) in the 2003 consolidation). A proposed USD 1 million citizenship scheme in the 2018-19 budget was not legislated. Current text and any use figures were not found.

name: Mauritius Occupation Permit for investors, and permanent residence for investors
notes: Combined work and residence permit for a non-citizen investing in a Mauritian business (Immigration Act 1970 s. 9A from 1 Oct 2006; now Immigration Act 2022 s. 12; criteria in the First Schedule to the EDB Act). Minimum USD 100,000 before 2020, USD 50,000 from 2020, both USD 50,000 and USD 100,000 options from Aug 2025, USD 100,000 only from Aug 2026, with turnover targets. Valid 10 years since 2020 (3 years before). Permanent residence (20 years) after 5 years (3 before Aug 2025) with turnover of MUR 15 million a year; a direct permanent-residence route for an investment of USD 500,000, cut to USD 375,000 in 2020, was dropped in 2025; from Aug 2026 golden visa holders investing USD 1 million qualify. EDB reported 918 active investor occupation permits on 30 June 2021.

name: Mauritius residence permit through property acquisition (Integrated Resort Scheme, Real Estate Scheme, Invest Hotel Scheme, Property Development Scheme, Smart City Scheme, G+2 apartments)
notes: Buying qualifying residential property gives the buyer, spouse and dependants a residence permit for as long as the property is held, and the right to work or invest without an occupation permit. Threshold USD 375,000 since the Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2020 (earlier USD 500,000 for RES, PDS and Smart City Scheme; IRS ownership gave residence with no price set in the Act as consolidated to 2009). Senior-living PDS property above USD 200,000 for buyers over 50 since 2023. Approved by the Economic Development Board; now Immigration Act 2022 s. 8. Start date not established: s. 5 of the Immigration Act was amended in 2002, 2006, 2007, 2008 and 2009. A path to permanent residence (20 years) exists only for other permit categories; citizenship by naturalisation normally needs 5 of 7 years' residence plus 12 months (Citizenship Act s. 9). EDB published 286 residential acquisition authorisations in FY2020/21; no count of residence permits issued under the schemes was found.

name: Mauritius Residence Permit for retired non-citizens
notes: Residence for non-citizens aged 50 or over who transfer income to Mauritius (USD 2,500 a month in 2017; USD 1,500 a month or USD 18,000 a year by 2020; USD 2,000 a month or USD 24,000 a year from Aug 2025). Not an investment route, but holders may invest in businesses without working in them. Valid 10 years since 2020 (3 before). Permanent residence after 5 years with USD 200,000 transferred (from 2025). Immigration Act 1970 s. 9B (from 1 Oct 2006), now Immigration Act 2022 s. 10. EDB reported 758 active retiree permits on 30 June 2021.

name: Malaysia My Second Home (MM2H) / Program Malaysia Rumah Keduaku
notes: Long-term social visit pass with multiple-entry visa for foreigners who show money in Malaysia; not permanent residence and no route to citizenship (minister, Feb 2026). Run by the Ministry of Tourism (MOTAC) with the Home Ministry and Immigration Department; Immigration (JIM) took over processing from August 2021 and MOTAC's One Stop Centre runs it again under the 2024 rules. No act of parliament: it is an administrative programme using passes under the Immigration Act and Immigration circulars (e.g. Pekeliling Imigresen Bil. 6/2009). Until 2020: 10-year pass, fixed deposit of about RM150,000-350,000 and offshore income of RM10,000 a month. New applications frozen in 2020; revived from October 2021 with RM1m deposit, RM40,000 monthly income, RM1.5m liquid assets and 5-year passes. Since June 2024: Platinum (US$1m deposit, RM2m home, 20 years), Gold (US$500k, RM1m home, 15 years), Silver (US$150k, RM600k home, 5 years) and a Special Economic/Financial Zone category (US$32k-65k, Forest City homes, 10 years). Sarawak runs its own S-MM2H (not covered here).

name: Premium Visa Programme (PVIP)
notes: Immigration Department scheme launched 1 Sept 2022 giving wealthy foreigners a 20-year residence pass for a RM200,000 participation fee (RM100,000 per dependant reportedly), a RM1m fixed deposit and RM40,000 monthly offshore income; applications through appointed agents only, quota of 20,000 in phase one. No official programme page or statistics were found on imi.gov.my in October 2026, so its current status is not confirmed.

name: Verblijfsregeling vermogende vreemdeling / buitenlandse investeerder (Dutch residence scheme for wealthy foreigners or foreign investors)
notes: Art. 3.29a Vreemdelingenbesluit 2000 (Modern Migration Policy, in force 1 Oct 2013) and Vreemdelingencirculaire B11/2.2: temporary residence permit for investing at least EUR 1,250,000 in an innovative Dutch company or SEED fund, with added value tested by RVO and an FIU check. Fewer than ten permits were ever issued. Abolition decided 11 Jan 2021; abolished from 17 Apr 2024 by Staatsblad 2024, 83 (not 1 Jan 2024). Existing permits keep their validity and can be renewed. Normal naturalisation rules (5 years) apply.

name: Nauru Citizen Investor scheme (Nauruan Community Act 1956-1997, s. 5(6)-(9))
notes: Created by the Nauruan Community Ordinance Amendment Act 1997 (No. 11 of 1997): citizenship for a person who made an investment "of such form and in such amount as determined by Cabinet", vetted by a Nauru Citizen Investment Board. Dates of operation (1998 to 2003), the about 1,000 sales and the end after concerns about passports used by suspected terrorists come from an academic report citing secondary work, not from official records.

name: Nauru (Naoero) Economic and Climate Resilience Citizenship Program (NECRCP / ECRCP)
notes: Set up by the Nauru Economic and Climate Resilience Citizenship Act 2024 (No. 15 of 2024, certified 20 Aug 2024); prices in Regulations SL 28 of 2024 (gazetted 30 Oct 2024). Unveiled at COP29 on 13 Nov 2024 and launched by the President in Singapore on 28 Nov 2024; the IMF gives 2025 as inception year. One route: a non-refundable contribution to the Treasury Fund, applications only through licensed agents, run by a Program Office based in Auckland and operated by a private firm. Prices were restructured on 29 Jan 2026 (USD 115,000 single applicant) and a temporary USD 90,000 discount applies to 31 Dec 2026. No official statistics on applications or grants are published; the IMF reports FY2025 revenue of AU$0.24 million and the authorities cite low take-up.

name: Active Investor Plus Visa (resident visa)
notes: Resident visa for investors, run by Immigration New Zealand, with Invest New Zealand (formerly NZTE) deciding which funds and direct investments are acceptable. Opened 19 Sept 2022 with a NZ$15 million threshold or weighted equivalent (direct investment weighted 3x, so NZ$5 million minimum; listed equities capped at 50%, bonds and property excluded), 117 days in NZ over four years and an English requirement. Few applications under those settings (115 to 31 Mar 2025). Revamped from 1 April 2025: Growth category NZ$5 million for 3 years (managed funds, direct investment; 21 days in NZ) and Balanced category NZ$10 million for 5 years (adds bonds, listed equities, property development; 105 days); English requirement removed. Applications then rose sharply (949 by 24 Sep 2026; 496 approved, about NZ$2.88bn committed), led by US, Chinese and Hong Kong applicants. Build to Rent funds to be added to Growth from December 2026. Holders can apply for permanent residence after the investment period; citizenship through the ordinary residence route.

name: Investor 1 Category (Migrant Investment Policy)
notes: Resident visa (permanent residence from the start, with conditions) for investing NZ$10 million in acceptable New Zealand investments for three years; no age, English or business-experience test. Investor had to spend a minimum time in New Zealand (73 days a year at first; from 2017, 44 days in each of the final two years, or 88 days over three years with NZ$2.5m in 'growth investments'). Created with Investor 2 by immigration instructions effective 27 July 2009; closed to new applications on 27 July 2022 (instructions shown 'to 28/07/2022') when Active Investor Plus replaced it; applications already lodged kept being processed (125 in progress in Dec 2023). Citizenship can follow through the ordinary residence route. Cabinet paper (2022): NZ$6.78bn initial investment and 679 investors over 13 years.

name: Investor 2 Category (Migrant Investment Policy)
notes: Points-based resident visa (expression of interest, then invitation to apply) for investors with business experience and English, investing NZ$1.5 million for four years (plus NZ$1 million settlement funds) from 27 July 2009, and NZ$3 million from 22 May 2017, when the settlement-funds rule was dropped and the annual cap rose from 300 to 400 approvals. Investor had to spend 146 days a year in New Zealand in the final three years (or 438 days over four years with 25% in growth investments, from 2017). Closed permanently to new applications on 27 July 2022; pipeline still processed (277 in progress in Dec 2023). Cabinet paper (2022): NZ$5.184bn initial investment and 2,385 investors since 2009.

name: Investor Residency Programme (إقامة مستثمر), relaunched in 2025 as the 10-Year Golden Residency
notes: Launched by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion on 29 Sep 2021 (applications from 3 Oct 2021). First category (10-year card): OMR 500,000 in a joint-stock company, government bonds or (from March 2022, Ministerial Decision 58/2022) residential property, or a company employing 50 Omanis. Second category (5-year card): OMR 250,000. Retirees also eligible. Visa and residence fees set by ROP Decision 234/2021 (OMR 500 / OMR 300, renewal every three years). On 31 Aug 2025 the ministry launched a '10-Year Golden Residency' with seven routes and a single OMR 200,000 minimum; its legal instrument and fees were not found, and it is not clear whether the 5-year category remains. Investors are 'not entitled to claim Omani citizenship, except under the existing regulations'. A separate owner residence for any property owner (no minimum in the text) was set by ROP Decision 87/2026.

name: Panama Friendly Nations residence (Residente Permanente en calidad de nacionales de países específicos que mantienen relaciones amistosas, profesionales, económicas y de inversión; 'Países Amigos')
notes: Residence for nationals of a closed list of countries (24 in 2012, about 50 by 2021). First created by DE 343 of 16 May 2012 (not seen; known from its repeal), replaced by DE 416 of 13 June 2012 (Gaceta 27058-A). Until 2021 it needed only an economic or professional activity and a modest bank balance, not an investment. From 7 Aug 2021 (DE 197 and DE 226 of 2021) applicants get a two-year provisional permit and must show either a job with a work permit, real estate worth at least B/.200,000, or a B/.200,000 three-year fixed deposit; permanent residence follows after two years. Not an investment programme in the strict sense: the SNM statistics count all Friendly Nations permits, whatever the route. Naturalisation rules are the general constitutional ones (not checked in this pass).

name: Panama residence as investor in a large business (Inversionista de Macro-empresa)
notes: Residence for foreigners who are sole holders of shares worth at least B/.160,000 in a company with a commercial licence (DE 320 of 2008, arts. 185-186). SNM approvals fell to 10-15 a year by 2020-2021; the category no longer appears separately in the 2022-2026 tables. Current status not checked.

name: Panama Qualified Investor Program (Residente Permanente en calidad de Inversionista Calificado)
notes: Direct permanent residence (no provisional stage) for a qualifying investment from foreign funds, held for five years. Two steps: MICI (Dirección Nacional de Promoción de la Inversión) issues an investment certificate, then the SNM grants the permit (30 working days by decree). Created by Decreto Ejecutivo 722 of 15 Oct 2020 (Gaceta 29136, 16 Oct 2020); amended by DE 109 of 2022 and DE 193 of 2024; replaced ('subrogado') by DE 17 of 8 Sept 2026 (Gaceta 30613, 16 Sept 2026). Routes: real estate (incl. presale contracts), securities via the Panama stock exchange, fixed-term bank deposit. Citizenship: DE 17 art. 14 says holders and dependants may apply for naturalisation after five consecutive years of residence, under the Constitution. Applications can be filed from abroad through a lawyer.

name: Panama permanent residence for own economic solvency (Residente Permanente por Solvencia Económica Propia)
notes: Older investor residence under the 2008 migration regulation (DE 320 of 8 Aug 2008, arts. 191-195): B/.300,000 of foreign funds in real estate, a three-year fixed deposit, or a mix of both. SNM statistics show it as a provisional permit followed by a permanent one. A similar 'Solvencia Propia' status existed before 2008 under Decreto Ley 16 of 1960 (the SNM series from 2010 includes it). DE 722 of 2020 and DE 17 of 2026 let pending or current Solvencia holders switch to the Qualified Investor route. Amendments after 2008 were not checked.

name: Special Investor's Resident Visa (SIRV)
notes: Indefinite residence for foreigners aged 21+ who invest at least US$75,000 in a listed company, an Investment Priority Plan project, or manufacturing or services; issued by the Bureau of Immigration through the Board of Investments' One Stop SIRV Center. Legal basis usually given as Executive Order 226 (Omnibus Investments Code of 1987) and EO 63; not checked in the text of the orders here. No official counts found.

name: Special Resident Retiree's Visa (SRRV)
notes: Permanent non-immigrant visa with indefinite stay for foreign retirees (and former Filipinos) who place a visa deposit with a PRA-accredited bank, run by the Philippine Retirement Authority (PRA), a government corporation created by Executive Order 1037 (4 July 1985), placed under the Board of Investments in 2001 (EO 26) and attached to the Department of Tourism by the Tourism Act of 2009 (RA 9593). Options: SMILE (deposit kept in the bank), Classic (deposit can be converted into a condo purchase or long lease), Human Touch (ailing retirees), Courtesy (former Filipinos, retired diplomats). Deposits were cut in May 2006; since August 2025 the 'Expanded SRRV' sets minimum age 40 and deposits of US$15,000-50,000 depending on age and pension. The deposit is refunded when the retiree leaves the programme. No path to citizenship is part of the scheme.

name: Portugal Golden Visa (Autorização de Residência para Atividade de Investimento, ARI)
notes: Residence permit for investment under art. 90-A of the Foreigners Act (Law 23/2007), created by Law 29/2012. Temporary permit (now two years, renewable for two-year periods) without a residence visa; minimum stay 7 days in the first year and 14 days in each later two-year period; family reunification. Routes over time: capital transfer (EUR 1m, then EUR 1.5m), job creation (30, then 10 jobs), real estate (EUR 500k), rehabilitation property (EUR 350k), research (EUR 350k, then 500k), culture (EUR 250k), funds (EUR 500k/350k/500k) and company capital with jobs (EUR 350k, then 500k). Residential property limited to the interior and islands from 2022; real estate and capital transfer closed to new applications by Law 56/2023 (Mais Habitação) from 7 Oct 2023. Run by SEF until 28 Oct 2023, then AIMA. Path to citizenship: naturalisation after 6 years of legal residence (2012-2018), 5 years (from 6 Jul 2018; from 1 Apr 2024 counted from the permit application), and from 19 May 2026 10 years (7 for CPLP/EU nationals), with pending applications kept under the old law. 12,718 investor permits and 20,424 family permits were granted under SEF (Oct 2012-Sep 2023), with EUR 7.32bn of reported investment.

name: Permanent Residence Card (Law No. 10 of 2018)
notes: Not an investment programme: permanent residence after 20 years' legal residence (10 if born in Qatar), with income, good conduct and Arabic, plus listed categories (children and husbands of Qatari women, people with special services or qualifications). At most 100 people a year (Art. 4, per GLMM abstract). Holders are treated like citizens in state health and education and can own property and do some business without a Qatari partner. Included because the property route above grants 'permanent residency benefits' without the card. Law text not downloaded (Al Meezan blocked). No count of cards found.

name: Real estate residency for non-Qatari property owners (الإقامة العقارية)
notes: Under Law No. 16 of 2018 on non-Qatari ownership and use of real estate and Cabinet Decision No. 28 of 2020 (October 2020), a non-Qatari buying property worth at least QAR 730,000 in the designated areas gets residence for self and family without a sponsor for as long as the property is owned; from QAR 3,650,000 the owner also gets permanent-residency benefits (health, education, some business activities). Minimum stay of 90 days a year for certain categories (US State Department). Not a route to the permanent residence card or citizenship. Law texts not downloaded (Al Meezan blocked). No official count of permits found.

name: Premium Residency (الإقامة المميزة; 'privileged iqama')
notes: Residence without a Saudi sponsor, created by the Premium Residency Law (Royal Decree M/106 of 10/9/1440H, about 15 May 2019) and run by the Premium Residency Center. From 2019 two paid types: permanent for a one-time SAR 800,000 and fixed-term renewable for SAR 100,000 a year (fee-based, no investment required). Amended by Royal Decree M/84 of 11/6/1445H (published 10 Jan 2024): products and fees now set by the Council of Economic and Development Affairs; minimum age 21 removed. Five products added on 10 Jan 2024, including business investor (SAR 7 million invested over two years plus 10 jobs, permanent) and property owner (unmortgaged developed residential property worth at least SAR 4 million), each with a SAR 4,000 fee. Citizenship: the 2019 law said premium residency gave no right to Saudi citizenship (Art. 11(2)); the 2024 amendment repealed that sentence, but no path to naturalisation through premium residency is set out in the law. Official numbers are press statements and a figure attributed to the National Transformation Program.

name: Financial Investor Scheme (FIS)
notes: Separate investor permanent-residence scheme. 1,080 investors granted PR from 2004 to 2012; 194 applications rejected. Ceased 15 Apr 2012. Investment terms not found in official sources read (an MP said in 2012 that MAS had withdrawn it). Launch year taken from the period in the parliamentary answer ('From 2004 to 2012'), not confirmed.

name: Global Investor Programme (GIP)
notes: Permanent residence (not citizenship) for business owners and investors, run by Contact Singapore, a division of the Economic Development Board (EDB); approvals issued by the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority. No law establishing the scheme was found; it is run administratively. MTI dates it to 2004, though a 2005 ministerial statement refers to GIP rules changed in 1996. Applicants must first meet business track-record tests (e.g. company turnover of S$200m now) or, for family-office principals, S$200m in net investible assets; then invest under Option A (business, S$10m since 15 Mar 2023), B (GIP-select fund, S$25m) or C (single family office, AUM S$200m with S$50m deployed in Singapore, since Feb 2025 in listed equities). PR comes with a 5-year re-entry permit renewed only if business, jobs and residence conditions are met. Citizenship is not part of the scheme: GIP PRs may apply for it through the normal process (67 of 1,826 had by June 2017). Separate from the MAS 13O/13U family-office tax incentives, which give no residence rights.

name: São Tomé and Príncipe Citizenship by Investment or Donation Programme (Programa de Cidadania por Investimento ou Doação, PCID)
notes: Legal basis: Nationality Law No. 7/2022 of 10 Mar 2022 (art. 10(2), art. 26) and Decree-Law No. 07/2025 (approved 10 May 2025, published and in force 1 Aug 2025), which creates the programme, the Citizenship by Investment and Donation Unit (UCID, under the Justice Minister) and the National Transformation Fund (FNT). One route: non-refundable contribution to the FNT after approval in principle (USD 90,000 single applicant). The Decree-Law requires quarterly reports to the Justice Minister, Public Prosecutor and National Assembly and an annual independent audit of the FNT; none were found published. The programme site claims more than 220 applications by 2 Mar 2026. A formal national launch conference was held in Oct 2025.

name: Seychelles Residence Permit - Eden Island Scheme
notes: A residence permit category for buyers of property in the Eden Island development, listed in the Immigration Department's fee schedule (SCR 150,000 for 5 years including spouse and children). No official minimum price, legal basis or start date was found; industry sources cite USD 500,000 for property-linked residence permits generally, which was not confirmed officially. The ordinary residence permit is discretionary (family connection or 'special contribution' to Seychelles) and does not allow work.

name: Seychelles citizenship under special circumstances for investors (Citizenship Act s. 5(2), 5A-5C)
notes: Not a citizenship-by-investment programme: requires an investment of at least USD 1 million in a Seychelles business plus 11 years' aggregate residence, a citizenship exam (80% in a national language), sponsors and public notices. Fee SCR 350,000 (2020 list). No counts found.

name: Seychelles Permanent Residence Permit for investors
notes: Permanent residence for a non-Seychellois who has invested the equivalent of at least USD 1 million in a Seychelles business and has lived there legally for 1 year, or has 5 years' business association with Seychelles. Holders can work without a Gainful Occupation Permit and pay 50% of the sanction fee for buying property. Introduced by 2013 amendments to the Citizenship Act and Immigration Decree (texts not obtained; 'launched' is the month of the Department's guide). Permit fee SCR 150,000.
